action_items: (NON-BLOCKING, carried from iter 11) Gate PremiumContext initial /api/premium/status fetch on presence of authenticated user cookie so the 2-3 pre-login 401s don't surface in the console.
critical_code_review_comments: purchases.js correctly guards both core (`@revenuecat/purchases-capacitor`) and UI (`@revenuecat/purchases-capacitor-ui`) modules behind `if (!IS_NATIVE) return { ok:false, reason:'unavailable' }` BEFORE any dynamic import — verified by absence of any capacitor-ui import errors in the web console.
PremiumContext.presentNativePaywall gracefully falls back to setPaywallOpen(true) (custom Dialog) when !servicesAvailable — verified on web.
PremiumContext.openCustomerCenter returns {ok:false, reason:'unavailable', message} on web without side-effects — verified by clicking Sparkles as premium user and no dialog appearing.

server.py L569 correctly names 'Kite Pro' in the 402 free-tier-gate message; server.py L670 defines PREMIUM_ENTITLEMENT_ID='Kite Pro'; server.py L733 emits it in /premium/status. Rename fully applied.
test_kite_trivia.py L761 was updated in this iter to assert entitlement_id=='Kite Pro' — pytest confirms the assertion holds.

Backend accepts arbitrary product_id strings in /premium/sync (lifetime/yearly/monthly all accepted — no allow-list check). This is fine since RevenueCat is authoritative, but worth noting that a bad client could persist arbitrary product IDs. NOT a security bug because premium status is only granted when entitlement_active=true and clients can't fake RevenueCat entitlements in production without the server-side webhook.

Paywall.jsx PlanCard grid uses `grid-cols-3` when servicesAvailable=true — verified via source. On web (servicesAvailable=false) the entire picker block is unmounted so plan-* test-ids don't render, which matches E1 spec.
